bookCredit: Prince Caspian by C. S. Lewis (1951) is quoted only in short lines.
title: Follow the Lion’s Shadow

banner.alt: A moonlit gorge with a stream, a path zigzagging up the far cliff to a hill with white rocks, and trees leaning in as if they were waking

keepsake.name: golden apple
keepsake.line: Only Imagination Trip travelers earn this one. From the moles’ orchard at Cair Paravel.

postcard.kicker: Nell · a page from my diary
body: Four to one, and she is the youngest. Still Lucy follows the Lion down into the gorge, and one by one the others begin to see him too.
Build the path he led them along.
postcard.word: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with a river at the bottom.

mission.h: Build Aslan’s path through the gorge
mission.p: The stream and its stepping stones, the hill with white rocks, the romp at the top.

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build in this order:
  1. the stream: stepping stones in a line
  2. the hill: white rocks, the moon above
  3. at the top: the Lion
  4. around him: vines and grapes
steps.say: Stand at the stream, where Edmund first saw him. Practice these 2 sentences:
steps.frame: “At the ___, ___ could see Aslan. That changed ___ because ___.”
steps.extra: Put a Barn Owl in a tree. When Aslan roared, owls hooted across Narnia.
steps.fits: the stones, the hill and the Lion

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less, shows the stepping stones, the white rocks, the Lion and the vines, and you say 2 sentences: one stop on the path, who could see Aslan there, and what changed, with a detail from Chapter 11.

alt.p: The night’s moments happen at four places along Aslan’s path. Put each one where it belongs.
alt.gameH: Tap a moment, then tap its place

spots.name: On the hill of the Stone Table

items.t: Lucy tells her story for the fourth time
items.why: A blank silence follows. Susan says she has been dreaming.

items.t: Trumpkin says he will follow the High King
items.why: His duty, he says, though he has no use for lions nobody can see.

items.t: Edmund spots a shadow crawling ahead
items.why: It is Aslan’s shadow. Edmund almost sees the Lion himself.

items.t: Aslan stops to drink, and Edmund sees him
items.why: He darts forward. Peter saw something too, and feels half as tired.
In a very small voice. She had believed, deep down, and would not let herself.

items.t: Trumpkin is tossed in the air and caught like a kitten
items.why: Safe as if he had been in bed, though he did not feel so. Then: shall we be friends?

items.t: The trees come bowing and dancing
items.why: After the roar: birch-girls, willow-women, oak-men, all shouting his name.

alt.miss: Not there. Think about how far along the path they had come when it happened.

write.q: Pick one stop on Aslan’s path: the camp, the way down, the stream, or the hill. In 2 sentences, say who could see Aslan there and what changed for them, with one detail from Chapter 11.

scripts.brief: Hello, dear. It’s Nell. In Chapter 11 it is four to one, and Lucy is the youngest, but she follows the Lion down into the gorge anyway. One by one the others begin to see him: Edmund at the stream, Peter soon after, Susan at last on the hill. Build the path Aslan led them along, from the stepping stones to the hill where the trees woke, and tell me what changed at one stop.
scripts.alt: No headset? Sit by my bench. The night’s moments happen at four places along Aslan’s path. Put each one where it belongs, and you will see how seeing him spread from one child to the next.
scripts.saved: The path is built, and the trees are dancing at the top. Here is your golden apple. Keep it, and remember that Susan did not need to say much.

testPara: At the stream, Edmund could see Aslan for the first time. That changed Peter too because he said three cheers for Lucy and did not feel half so tired.
